g.title: rp_daemon
g.text: CHARRA v2 — Relying Party, daemon mode
The RP's own states run down the
of the page. Each peer box sits on the
as the RP state that calls it,
reached by a dashed link — on whichever side keeps the wiring clear, so read the line, not the side. Peers are coloured by party:
— distinct key pairs, though in this PoC both live in the same TPM simulator. Diamonds are guards; red edges are failure paths. Red notes inside a box mark a
" in section 3 — drawn as a connector, not a wire, so five failure paths do not become five parallel lines.
command-line flag the RP process is started with
— a local setting, never a protocol message; the value beside it is this diagram's example, not a fixed constant.

g.title: cluster_cycle
g.text: — run_one_attestation_cycle(). Benchmark mode runs this same body, but a failed cycle is FATAL there; only the daemon treats it as one lost cycle.

g.title: cluster_idle
g.text: — the wait between one attestation cycle and the next.
The RP has no attestation work here, so instead of sleeping straight through the gap,
it spends it renewing whatever is about to expire. Each renewal fires on its own credential's
deadline, not on the loop cadence — that is what decouples the renew margins from --interval.

g.title: TM1
g.text: ⚠ answer is unauthenticated: no signature, no nonce

g.title: A0
g.text: ① FETCH — RP reads from the Attester:
the RP needs this leg because, unlike a Verifier, it has no request
from the subject to learn EK_a and AK_a from
② ACTIVATE — RP challenges, the Attester answers:
MakeCredentials a fresh 32-byte random secret against
Only TPM_a can recover it, and the
Attester echoes it back to the RP.
a wrong length counts as a mismatch
③ DELIVER_RP — only now does the RP sign:
and nothing is written to the RP's issuance ledger, until the echo
matches. The certificate then travels in the clear
Same ordering as the Verifier's own /certify_ak — proof, then issuance — so all
three certification relationships in the system now behave alike. The RP's ACTIVATE
and the relayed Verifier one are the same request kind; the Attester cannot tell
them apart, and does not need to.

g.title: A1
g.text: ① Attester ensures its own EK_a + AK_a exist (cached)
② Attester opens its TPM and loads AK_a
PCRs from its IMA log. PCRs 0–15 cannot be reset, so
repeating it would keep growing PCR 10 and no replay of the
log would reproduce it — later calls skip straight to ④
④ Attester runs TPM2_Quote, signed by AK_a,
⑤ Attester returns Quote_a + log + AK_a certificates

g.title: A2
g.text: it — INFO on accept, ERROR on reject.
Nothing is persisted and nothing acts on it. On a real base station
this is the hook that would drive an alert or a re-measurement.

g.title: V0
g.text: default port 31415; run at 5684+ per verifiers_config.txt
The subject is bound into the pending challenge and picks which issuance
ledger the record lands in. The Verifier refuses to guess — mixing the two
is exactly what that field exists to prevent.
Both subjects run the same two legs:
Verifier i validates that subject's EK certificate
manufacturer root, then challenges: TPM2_MakeCredential against
Not the only EK check in the system — the RP runs the same
chain validation on EK_a before minting its own certificate (see Phase 1),
and challenges TPM_a the same way before issuing. See that box.
the TPM that owns the EK activates the credential
echoed back — the RP itself for SUBJECT_RP, the
SUBJECT_ATTESTER, where the RP only relays
that AK's certificate under its own CA

g.title: V1
g.text: Before an RP may redact real Attester evidence, it must prove
it runs the correct, unmodified PATH_Clean SDK — the path-mapping
module that turns a real path into its redacted form.
① fabricates a synthetic IMA log from a random seed
② redacts it ITSELF with a random salt → the golden answer,
and replays that to a golden PCR digest
③ sends the RP the RAW log + the salt — never the golden answer
who is this — three bindings, all required:
· its serial is still live in this Verifier's AK ledger
· the DER public key sent beside it
is the key inside that certificate
without this last one the certificate is merely an attachment: the submitter
could staple someone else's certificate to a key of its own choosing
the signature over the submitted PCR
the key: every AK in CHARRA is created with TPM2_ALG_RSAPSS/SHA-256 in its
template, so that is the only scheme its TPM will sign under, and the Verifier
Signed data here is the 32-byte PCR digest
Freshness comes from the challenge instead: fresh seed and salt per /qualify,
and spent on first use. This signature authenticates
⑥ the RP's redacted log must equal the golden log BYTE FOR BYTE,
and its PCR digest must equal the golden PCR digest
⑦ all three ⇒ qualified for the validity window, recorded in the
ledger shared by every Verifier instance, so one answer serves all.
The challenge is spent either way — a retry needs a fresh /qualify
The golden comparison is on log + digest, never on signature bytes: RSA-PSS
salting makes two honest signings over identical data differ. The shared salt is
the one deliberate exception to never transmitting it — safe only because this
the SDK takes ONE salt for the whole log here, because byte-identical
reproduction is only possible that way. Real evidence takes the other branch —
a fresh salt per entry. Same function, so the exam proves the RP holds the right
path-mapping module, but it never exercises the per-entry salt path itself.
the spec has the Verifier PUSH test logs to the RP periodically.
Here the RP PULLS a challenge when its grant expires — same check, inverted
initiator; the period comes from the RP's expiry + renew margin, not a Verifier timer.
The SDK itself is never distributed either: it is compiled into both binaries.

g.title: V2
g.text: the same request it sent the Attester
the RP's nonce, to check Quote_a's
with a nonce IT chose — a value the RP
picked itself would prove nothing about Quote_r's freshness
Asymmetry: Quote_r answers a Verifier-chosen nonce, Quote_a only
the Verifier about. Step 3b freshness is
therefore RP-asserted — a dishonest RP could replay an old Quote_a
together with its matching old nonce.

g.title: V3
g.text: ① AK_r certificate chains to this Verifier's CA
still live in this Verifier's AK ledger
revocation mechanism, since EKs are not re-checked here
①b this RP holds a valid qualification
RSA-PSS/SHA-256 again, but over (PCR_r ‖ this Verifier's nonce) — so unlike
/qualify_submit's, this one IS freshness-bound by what it covers
③ the nonce it issued comes back, single-use
① AK_a certificate — chain + ledger, same as ① above
② Quote_a signature under AK_a, verified
once by the TPM, once by mbedTLS. Step 3a ② has no such
second opinion — PCR_r never was in a TPM to begin with
③ the RP's nonce comes back in Quote_a
3a AND 3b — both always run, so one
reply lists every reason it failed
log_r is received and never checked.
replay, no comparison against PCR_r — the Verifier accepts PCR_r purely
on RP's signature over it. Log content is the RP's Step 2a job, run on
the raw log before redaction, and the Verifier does not re-do it.
the spec's item 1 says "EK and AK certificates". Only the AK
certificate is checked here; EK_r and EK_a were chain-validated once at
certification, and the EK↔AK binding is carried by ActivateCredential.

g.title: CLI
g.text: RP parses its own command line
the window on the certificate the RP mints in Phase 1

g.title: NOTATION
g.text: EK_a / AK_a, EK_r / AK_r endorsement + attestation keys
TPM_a / TPM_r each party's TPM (one simulator here)
log_a the Attester's raw measurement log
log_r the same log after the RP redacts every path
Quote_a / Quote_r the signed (PCR, nonce) pair from each
PCR_r the PCR digest a replay of log_r produces
the per-entry digest IMA stores in the log, over
that entry's template_data (its algorithm, file digest and path)
when a check cannot be completed the answer is NO,
a failure here does not stop the cycle

g.title: ENTER
g.text: without --duration there is no deadline at all and every check on it below
is skipped — the daemon then stops only on --cycles or an operator stop request (Ctrl-C / SIGTERM)

g.title: CYC
g.text: RP starts a cycle · asks for Verifier IDs 1..N

g.title: GETV
g.text: timeout is a fixed 30 s built into the RP — not --verifier-timeout,
and there is no flag for it

g.title: ATTID
g.text: RP certifies the Attester under the RP's own CA
a valid AK_a certificate already held
→ nothing to do, the RP moves straight on
the RP FETCHes the Attester's identity, checks EK_a
challenges TPM_a and waits for the
, and only then mints and delivers the certificate
The cache is a file on disk, so this normally runs once per deployment,
not once per process — and again when the certificate nears expiry
(--ak-renew-margin), which the idle window also watches for.

g.title: MKREQ
g.text: fresh nonce, chosen by the RP

g.title: STEP2A
g.text: Step 2a · RP appraises the Attester's evidence itself
① AK_a certificate the RP issued ② Quote_a signature under AK_a
③ the RP's nonce came back ④ log self-consistency
⑤ replayed PCR digest ⑥ file-hash policy — all six always run

g.title: RESULT
g.text: the RP reports its verdict, only when it reached one

g.title: STEP2B
g.text: Phase 3 · Step 2b · RP redacts the evidence, ONCE per cycle
RP rewrites every path in the Attester's log:
redacted_path = SHA256(path ‖ fresh random salt), a new salt per entry
→ irreversible even against guessed paths, and repeated paths cannot be correlated
RP recomputes each entry's template_hash — it must equal SHA256 of the
new template_data, or log_r fails its own self-consistency check
PCR_r is computed in SOFTWARE by replaying log_r — not a real
TPM2_Quote over live PCRs. See the signing box below.
the salts are random, so redacting again would hand
each Verifier a different log_r for one and the same attestation

g.title: QUAL
g.text: · the RP sits the access check
only reached on a cache miss or expiry. The RP tries Verifiers in order and
stops at the first verdict — the ledger is shared, so the answer would be the
same everywhere. Only a TRANSPORT failure (or an AK_r certificate it could not
get from that Verifier) moves to the next candidate; a local redact, replay or
sign failure abandons the search outright.
RP first gets AK_r certified by that Verifier
rejects an unknown submitter, so on a cold start the very first
/certify_ak happens HERE, not in the threads below (they find it cached)
① RP asks that Verifier for a challenge
② RP redacts the synthetic log it was handed, using the salt it
was given — the same SDK function real evidence goes through, though
in its one-salt-for-the-whole-log mode; see the Verifier box
③ RP replays its result into a PCR digest and signs that digest with
④ RP submits log + digest + signature +
AK_r certificate — the key and the certificate both, so the Verifier

g.title: FORK
g.text: RP forks one thread per Verifier

g.title: TRESET
g.text: RP thread i clears Verifier i's vote to FALSE
fail-closed: no stale PASS survives into this vote

g.title: VOTE
g.text: RP counts the votes — strict majority

g.title: CYCDONE
g.text: either verdict completes it — a lost vote is a
, not a cycle failure; the daemon carries on

g.title: TCERT1
g.text: held and not near expiry → skipped, no round trip
On a cold start this is normally already cached: qualification needed AK_r
certified by this same Verifier and did it first, upstream of the fork.
best-effort — the RP forwards the evidence either way

g.title: TCERT2
g.text: held and not near expiry → skipped, no round trip
Four legs rather than three: the CA and the subject cannot talk directly, so the
RP couriers the challenge and the echo between them. Same proof-then-issue order.
③ RP returns the Attester's answer to
④ RP delivers the certificate to

g.title: TNONCE
g.text: the RP sends the same request it sent the Attester,
and Verifier i answers with a nonce of its own

g.title: TBUILD
g.text: RP thread i signs and assembles the evidence for Verifier i
signs (PCR_r ‖ Verifier i's nonce) with AK_r → Quote_r
each Verifier issued its own nonce, so
each signature is over different bytes
— log_r replaces it. Sending the raw log
would defeat the redaction entirely, so Evidence_a' is Quote_a alone.
"a TPM-certified identity signed this PCR_r for this
nonce" — not "the TPM attests this PCR_r", since PCR_r is a replay.

g.title: TAPPR
g.text: one attempt — the answer is a vote, not a retry

g.title: TVOTE
g.text: PASS only if Verifier i replied \"Attestation successful!\"

g.title: CYCFAIL
g.text: ▸ abort — every abort connector lands here
a peer briefly unreachable costs the RP one cycle, not the process

g.title: SHUT
g.text: RP releases the last cycle's evidence buffers
and tears down its CoAP context

g.title: NAP
g.text: RP naps for min(--interval, time left on --duration)

g.title: IDLEQ
g.text: nap over, or asked to stop?

g.title: RENEW
g.text: RP renews whatever is close to expiring
skipped entirely when that margin is 0 — re-qualifying then falls back
inside the next attestation, which is what the margin exists to avoid
· its own AK_r certificate from each Verifier
· the Attester's AK_a certificate from each Verifier
each call re-checks its own cache first, so a pass with nothing due is free.
Same endpoints the cycle uses, reached from the idle window.

g.title: WAKE
g.text: RP sleeps only until the next renewal falls due

g.title: SLEEP
g.text: nothing is polled or awaited here — the slicing exists only so that a
is acted on within a second, instead of after
the whole (possibly minutes-long) sleep has run its course
